verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents token-based API keys and bot tokens that act for a machine rather than a user, which suits agent credentials. Saying keys have Owner permissions 'by default' implies permissions can be changed, but the pack never shows how to restrict or scope a key. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of per-key permission scoping or role assignment, least-privilege or read-only key options, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: An API key can perform actions like any other user, and by default, it will have Owner permissions.
FireHydrant supports bot tokens to act on behalf of a computer instead of a user's account.
FireHydrant allows you to access the API with an API key using token-based authentication.
